title: Bean root rot and wilt - Sri Lanka

Header: Bean root rot and wilt - Sri Lanka
Fusarium oxysporum ; Fusarium solani In Sinhala – “Bonchi mul kunuweema ha melaweema”; In Tamil – Bonchi ver Alucal

Prevention: Deep plough to improve soil drainage.
Apply lime (2 t/ha) to increase soil pH at least two weeks before planting.
Prepare narrow and raised beds for planting.
Mix rice husk charcoal (3-5 kg/m2) at land preparation.
Use treated seeds (see yellow direct control).
Avoid excessive use of fertilizers, especially nitrogen.
Crop rotation with non-legumes can help prevent the disease.
Avoidance of drought stress also helps to prevent the disease as drought stressed plant are more susceptible.
Monitoring: Initially the margins of mature leaves become yellowish green.
Then the whole leaf will turn yellow and drop off.
These symptoms appear progressively on older leaves and sometimes the whole vine may die.
Look for dark brown discoloration of the vascular system in a split stem.
In severely infected plants the pith and cortical tissues are invaded by the fungus.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Thiophanate methyl 70% WP with 1 kg of seeds).
Thiophanate- methyl 70% WP; 30 g/50 l of water for 10m2.
Do not drench when rain iminent.
